topic: Your brain's best guess 7: They probably like you more than you think
caption:
You walk out of the meeting replaying the one thing you said wrong.

It can leave you sure they didn’t like you as much as you liked them. After group conversations and teamwork, people tended to underestimate how much others liked them. They probably like you more than you think, and the replay may be part of why: we tend to go back over the moments we think went badly.

After your next chat, try noticing one thing that probably went well.

Your brain's best guess is our series on everyday predictions that research suggests are often too pessimistic. Studies were in the US, with students talking in small groups, student engineering teams and working adults, so results may differ for you.

Research: Mastroianni, A. M., Cooney, G., Boothby, E. J., & Reece, A. G. (2021). The liking gap in groups and teams. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 162, 109-122. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.obhdp.2020.10.013
